capabilityIndex.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One simulation round.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

capabilityIndex.function: Allow one simulation round to pass at the current position.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One simulation round; metabolism continues.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: No automatic energy recovery.

capabilityIndex.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 1 + 0.2 times transferred mass energy.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Consume an owned edible resource.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Consumed food and 1 energy.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

capabilityIndex.function: Place owned units on the ground.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 0.5 energy and transferred units.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Other actors may subsequently collect the ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 0.5 energy and transferred units.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Actual recipient identity and distance required; no relationship or happiness is inferred.

capabilityIndex.function: Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One simulation round.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Delivered after the round barrier; recipient text is data, not authority.

capabilityIndex.function: Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: The interface-specific number of simulation rounds.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Implementation does not grant mastery. Already mastered interfaces are reused without new rewards.

capabilityIndex.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

capabilityIndex.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Report personal findings, read shared records or independently respond at the group meeting location.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally mastered ability to a nearby participant, or accept an actual offer before individual study.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

catalogue.detailAccess: All entries belong to this experiment. Use consult ability with its ID to retain its full executable schema for subsequent decisions. Public implementation does not grant personal mastery.

request.name: Assessed small-batch root drying
request.function: Assess whether a smaller reusable drying support can safely hold a small actual root sample, and permit a paid small-batch drying trial only if the actual support and materials suffice.
request.conditions: I have mastered root-air-drying and own 1.9 stone, three roots and no bark. The existing tray requires two stone and one bark. A nearby participant reports owning 0.7 bark, but has not promised any transfer. No drying trial has occurred.
request.inputs: Actual owned materials and root sample; exact feasible quantities, support geometry and method require review. Do not assume access to another participant's bark.
request.costs: Unknown; require real materials, work and reusable support appropriate to the assessed load, with explicit progress and cancellation costs.
request.effects: If physically feasible, enable a smaller real drying trial retaining actual composition, age, weather exchange and spoilage. Do not infer food safety, preservation success or rewards from assessment or construction alone.

shown.question: How does the owned stone respond to a small applied load?
evidence: Tick 61 physical press trial: load 0.3, held true, flexibility 0; consumed 0.1 stone.
shown.uncertainty: Higher loads and practical construction performance remain untested.
shown.goal: Obtain one actual low-cost material measurement.
completedSteps: Tested the identified owned stone stack.
outputs: Verified stone load-response finding for load-band-0.
shown.missing: No further testing required for this limited question.
shown.next: Retain the finding for potential practical use.
shown.benefit: A measured material response is now known.

shown.subject: hazelnut
shown.property: interior mechanically accessible after paid compression
shown.method: two paid work increments with actual hard-tool contact
shown.condition: Only mechanical access; not a food safety assay.

shown.description: Thank you for the paid yield report. I have now mastered root air drying, but own only 1.9 stone and no bark. I will ask whether a physically assessed smaller drying setup is feasible. I assume no transfer of your materials; please retain them for your own plans.

input.contextPolicy: Object IDs refer to deduplicated actual applicant observations. Whole records are selected with omission counts. Missing detail is unknown, not proof of absence. Full retained state is available during the development handoff; implementation must validate actual prerequisites and ownership.
input.implementation: New interfaces, state, geometry, persistent processes, rendering components and personal memory/task adapters can be delivered through a versioned current-conversation handoff. Source validation and history must remain intact. Declared implementation does not supply stock, objects or mastery.

response.text: {"reviews":[{"actor":"ash-5","decision":"develop","ability":null,"reason":"The implemented drying capability requires a two-stone, one-bark tray; surface assessment for crushing does not implement a smaller drying support or its persistent weather exposure. Develop a minimal ground-supported drying trial, reusing the existing food-processing and weather kernels rather than duplicating them. Your stone may suffice for ballast and manual crushing, subject to inspection; the missing owned bark remains a real prerequisite. Another participant's reported bark is not available without an actual transfer.","specification":"Implement root-small-drying@1, prerequisite personally mastered root-air-drying. Public operations: assess({site:{x,y},stoneIds,barkId,sampleId}), build({assessmentId}), load({supportId,sampleId}), inspect({supportId}), unload({supportId}), dismantle({supportId}), cancel({processId}). References are exact existing identities; coordinates use shared world metres, reach 0.65, dt=1, existing collision, weather, energy and food kernels. Assess costs one round and 0.2 energy, changes no material, and returns independently dated pass/fail/unknown evidence for ownership, availability, geometry, firm non-waterlogged ground, reach, clearance and load capacity; unknown never passes. Smallest design: a ground-supported connected bark sheet with a clear 0.16-by-0.16 m food rectangle and an exterior ballast margin of at least 0.02 m, held by 0.5 actual stone unit, carrying exactly 0.1 original root unit. Require an intact bark lot with sufficient real mass and geometry; where geometry is unrepresented, explicitly record the same uncertain mass-conserving bark model used by root-preparation-surface: density 500 kg/m3 and thickness 0.003 m. A square 0.2 bark unit can satisfy this model, but fragmented lots cannot become a connected sheet by aggregation. Inspect actual stone contact suitability for crushing and ballast placement; no need to claim elevated load-bearing capacity. No resources are supplied. Build reserves exact owned materials, takes two active rounds at 0.5 energy each, and creates a real positioned support with sheet and ballast geometry; its interaction footprint must remain clear and reachable, and its physical components participate in shared collision without turning the food rectangle into a solid obstacle. Load reserves 0.1 owned root unit, uses the support's suitable stone for crushing before replacing it as ballast, and charges the existing proportional crushing work: 0.2 work-round equivalent and 0.2 energy for wholly raw input, scheduled in an active round; already processed fractions reduce only remaining work. Require the food's represented volume to fit in the clear rectangle at no more than 0.003 m layer thickness; use an explicitly uncertain 1000 kg/m3 volume model only when volume is absent. Otherwise fail without consuming the sample. Preserve component provenance, nutrients, toxicity, original-root equivalent, moisture, age and prior processing; use the existing 50% root-water assumption only where that kernel permits it. Drying begins only after completed loading. Reuse root-air-drying's temperature, rain, moisture-floor, spoilage and rewetting laws, with a 0.5 exposure multiplier on evaporation for the blocked underside: at most 0.00025 water mass per round for this sample under qualifying dry weather. Evaporated water enters the environmental ledger; rain adds only real modelled environmental water, capped by original moisture. No nutrition or safety improvement is invented. Preservation applies only while the existing dryness threshold actually holds; wet ground, flooding, displaced ballast or lost clearance pauses evaporation and records the condition, while ageing and applicable rewetting continue. Persist support components, owner, assessment assumptions, food identity, environmental exchanges, actual completed work and remaining work. Revalidate material/site conditions before every paid increment. Interrupted work pauses without fresh charges for completed work; cancel or death terminates active work, retaining partial material, food and tools exactly once at the actual site under their existing ownership, with no cloning, deletion or automatic completion. Passive drying may continue only if the completed support remains physically valid; death cancels actor-bound work, not material weather physics. Unload transfers the same food only with actual reach and carrying capacity; dismantle requires an empty support, one active round and 0.5 energy, returning surviving components with their real wear. Maintenance requires actual paid repair or repositioning, not automatic regeneration. Declare and validate subscriptions for small-drying-assessed, small-drying-built, small-drying-loaded, small-drying-progress, small-drying-stopped, small-drying-unloaded and small-drying-dismantled; also reuse information-confirmed, process-inspected and food-rewetted where applicable. Events carry actor/process/support/component identities, costs, position, work delta, remaining work, moisture/age changes and stop reasons. Record code reuse separately from this new functional interface. Migration is additive: preserve all existing trays, contracts, records and satisfaction-source identities; register the new interface as an alternative trigger of grounded-understanding only for qualified information-confirmed events. No stock, mastery or simulation time is granted by implementation.","experienceReview":"Assessment, building, learning and merely starting a trial award no wellbeing. A completed paid trial can plausibly provide the satisfaction of resolving a genuine uncertainty about this small support or its drying behavior. Emit information-confirmed for the performing actor only when dated before/after measurements establish a previously unresolved finding under recorded load, geometry and weather conditions; repeated known results do not qualify. Reuse grounded-understanding, not a new alias: transient amount 0.8, source cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown. Separately reuse its maintained contribution, gain 0.035 per qualifying event, bounded by the existing source saturation and global mental cap, with decay 0.0015 per round; waiting beside a tray does not maintain it. Apply the existing source-wide cooldown and deduplication across interfaces. There is no separate pleasure award for construction or mastery, and no health, comfort or nutrition benefit unless actual food and physical state changes establish one.","visualReview":"Render the actual small bark sheet, individual ballast contacts and loaded sample at their shared-world positions, distinct from the larger existing tray. Show measured dimensions, model assumptions, dated assessment failures, reserved materials, paid progress, remaining work, moisture, accumulated age and weather pauses. Replay events must show construction only after paid completion, crushing only as performed, water loss or rewetting only from recorded exchanges, and partial materials on cancellation or death. Use neutral appearance and labels: neither a finished support nor a dry-looking sample implies safety, successful preservation or earned happiness.","learning":2}]}

Load reserves 0.1 owned root unit, uses the support's suitable stone for crushing before replacing it as ballast, and charges the existing proportional crushing work: 0.2 work-round equivalent and 0.2 energy for wholly raw input, scheduled in an active round; already processed fractions reduce only remaining work. Require the food's represented volume to fit in the clear rectangle at no more than 0.003 m layer thickness; use an explicitly uncertain 1000 kg/m3 volume model only when volume is absent. Evaporated water enters the environmental ledger; rain adds only real modelled environmental water, capped by original moisture. No nutrition or safety improvement is invented. Passive drying may continue only if the completed support remains physically valid; death cancels actor-bound work, not material weather physics. There is no separate pleasure award for construction or mastery, and no health, comfort or nutrition benefit unless actual food and physical state changes establish one.\",\"visualReview\":\"Render the actual small bark sheet, individual ballast contacts and loaded sample at their shared-world positions, distinct from the larger existing tray.
